title: Shell scripting: processes, input, and control flow
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Intel ARK page for the i5-12450H could not be opened for this chapter (the server returned a 555-byte refusal to scripted clients on 2026-10-26). The hybrid layout (4 P-cores x 2 threads, 4 E-cores x 1 thread, 12 threads) is taken from the authoring brief, which cites ARK; the chapter uses it only as a description of the machine and relies on no claim from it. Local evidence: nproc = 12, lscpu = 6 cores x 2 threads (synthetic WSL view).

POSIX text is the 2018 edition (IEEE Std 1003.1-2017, Issue 7); the page states that a newer edition exists. Only the test utility of the newer edition (POSIX.1-2024, Issue 8) was read, for the operators s1 > s2 and s1 < s2 and its rationale; the rest of the newer edition was not read, so the chapter does not claim that the other cited wording (for example the unspecified result for a '#!' first line, section 2.1) is unchanged there. The HTML pages carry section numbers but no page numbers; section numbers are cited.

The Bash manual cited is version 5.3 (18 May 2025), read as extracted HTML text. Every statement used from it was also run on Bash 5.2.21 (the version on the machine). Behaviours of Bash 5.3 that differ from 5.2.21 were not looked for.

execve(2) is Linux man-pages 6.19 (2026-02-08) and ld.so(8) is Linux man-pages 6.19 (2026-08-03), both read as extracted text from man7.org; the kernel on the machine is 6.6.87.2 (WSL 2). The 255-character and 127-character interpreter-line limits are quoted from the man page and were not tested.

The GCC manual 'Environment Variables' page was read on 2026-10-26; the page carries no version number. The local test (INCLUDE_PATH ignored, CPATH honoured) used gcc 13.3.0. The chapter makes no claim about other compilers' variables.

The Slurm sbatch manual is the page of version 26.05 as served on 2026-10-26. No scheduler exists on the machine, so the statements about #SBATCH lines and --export are the manual's, not tested. Chapter 30 treats schedulers.

Process counts in (5.5) come from a PID-difference probe (consecutive PIDs; each probe consumes one PID). It is exact only on a quiet system. It gave 4, 3, 1, 0 in every one of five runs, and 1, 1, 0, 3 for a substitution with a builtin, an external program, a plain assignment and a two-stage pipeline in three runs. Counts were not checked with a tracer (strace is not installed) and apply to Bash 5.2.21 only.

Timing: the printed fork_cost.sh sample was captured with code_lab.run_program through the private assembly script. The later runs of code_lab.py --chapter 5 passed and produced new samples that were not pasted. Quoted ranges come from four runs of the same script before final assembly (lecture loop 0.67-1.66 s, kappa 0.59-0.81 ms, awk 0.001-0.003 s, builtin true 1.4-2.5 us each); exercise 6 quotes three runs of a separate script (assignment 0.012-0.015 s per 1e4, $(echo hi) 4.4-5.8 s per 1e4, $(/bin/echo hi) 0.95-1.9 s per 1e3). A direct measurement of the awk program of fork_cost.sh on 1e6 generated lines took 0.285, 0.301 and 0.365 s (an empty awk BEGIN{} took 0.002 s); it is not a listing. These runs are not reproduced by listings; per-iteration timing under WSL 2 varied by a factor of up to 2.5 between runs.

The solver iteration counts 163, 515, 1657, 5272 and 16148 (N = 8..128 at tol 1e-6, max_iter 100000) and the times 0.02 s (N = 64) and 0.28 s (N = 128) quoted in the sweep section and in exercise 5 come from one ad hoc run of the solver source of sweep.sh built with gcc -O2, not from a listing. Review round 1 added: N = 256 gave 45651 iterations in 3.63 s and N = 512 gave 108997 iterations in 51.4 s (one run each by the author, solver of sweep.sh, no iteration limit, gcc -O2). N = 1024 gave 193751 iterations and 677 s in one run by the reviewer on a loaded machine; the author did not repeat it. Exercise 5 uses the growth factor 3.1 as an estimate and checks it against these runs; the factors per doubling are 3.22, 3.18, 3.06, 2.83, 2.39, 1.78. The reason for the falling factor (stopping test on the last change) and for the rising time per update (cache) are not tested.

The 20-digit input that defeats a digits-only check (section on exit status) was run in a separate test of a first version of grade_checked.sh; the final listing contains the length-limited version and its rejection of that input.

Round 1 disclosure: in the first version of the chapter the gcc session of the PATH section was edited: it omitted the lines of caret and 'compilation terminated.' and the echo of the status. The session now shows the command with echo "status $?" and the full gcc 13.3 output as run.

ENOEXEC behaviour (section script): a file plain.sh without an interpreter line that prints $BASH_VERSION gave 5.2.21(1)-release under ./plain.sh from Bash, an empty value (dash) under env ./plain.sh and under find -exec, and OSError Errno 8 under Python subprocess.run; xargs was not tested. execvp(3) was read for the /bin/sh statement. sbatch behaviour without a #! line was not tested.
Special built-ins ahead of functions (POSIX 2.9.1): tested with a function named export (accepted by bash, rejected by bash --posix as a special builtin).
Exit status 65 (EX_DATAERR) for bad input data of the checked grading script and 64 (EX_USAGE) for bad command-line arguments of the solver were checked in the local sysexits.h.

Word count: the first report of about 6600 words was wrong because the counting regular expression for math removed too much text. A corrected count (tags removed, math replaced by one token, code blocks excluded; tables, exercises, solutions and the source list included) is about 14000 words, in line with the reviewer's 13200. The brief's 6000 to 9000 is exceeded; no padding paragraph was found.
Forward reference: the model section refers to chapter 2 for fork, exec and wait; chapter 2 is not in the repository at the time of writing. Check at assembly.

ASR errors in the machine transcripts corrected from slides and subject: 'cell script' = shell script; 'C bank' / 'see bank' = shebang; 'SSL' = sh; 'ZS cell' = zsh; 'uco' = echo; 'dollar and this sign' = $?; 'dot psi' = ':$PATH'; 'usage greater than or equal to 3 short' = '-ge $THRESHOLD'; 'SDA1' = /dev/sda1; 'variable four dot SS' = var4.sh; 'peter' / 'pitter' = 'Pitter' (slide).

Slide errors: the code box of var2.sh and var4.sh shows '!/bin/bash' without '#' (frames f0042, f0045, f0047, f0049 and f0052 of W2L1) while the terminal capture shows '#!/bin/bash'; the code box of the while-loop slide shows 'Done' with a capital D (frames f0036, f0039, f0042 and f0044 of W2L2) while the terminal capture shows 'done'. The speech at W2L2 13:04 says 'greater than or equal to 5' for the test of 90. The chapter reads the code from the terminal captures.

The lectures were recorded on a system with the prompt root@localhost (user root); the chapter's runs are as an ordinary user on Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL 2. On the guest's /mnt/c (9p, no metadata) chmod has no effect, so all permission-bit listings use mktemp -d under /tmp.

Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times and locate topic changes to within a few seconds. The W2L1 duration is 2093 s from playlist.txt (the transcript header says 2092 s).
lecture_corrections: env lists only the exported variables (the environment), not all variables set in the shell (W2L1 about 18:33; env_demo.sh).
The explanation of the long variable list by 'everything is a file' (W2L1 about 19:06) is not supported; the environment is inherited at exec (execve(2); Bash manual 3.7.4).
The slide's export PATH=/home/master/Desktop:$PATH prepends; the speech says append or prepend (W2L1 about 28:38); position decides which program runs (path_demo.sh).
INCLUDE_PATH (slide) is not read by gcc 13.3; CPATH is (session in the PATH section; GCC manual).
The condition of if is the exit status of a command, not a Boolean value (W2L2 0:06); an error status counts as false.
'==' inside [ ] is a Bash extension and fails in dash; '>' is a redirection; signs cannot replace -gt in general (W2L2 about 6:59; status_demo.sh).
return carries only an eight-bit status: add 200 100 returns 44 (W2L2 about 27:21; functions_demo.sh).
The recursive factorial is correct only for n up to 20 (21 wraps, 66 gives 0) and creates one subshell per call (W2L2 about 29:27).
The while loop of the monitoring script does not monitor continuously; it checks each line of one df table once (W2L2 about 36:11; monitor.sh).
The lecture's grading script grades invalid input as C with status 0 (W2L2 about 11:30; read_demo.sh).
